predecessors.note: The Robertian duchy of Francia (eu-07-x dossier) became the Capetian domain when Hugh Capet was crowned in 987.

land.text: 'by the sixteenth century the "royal domain" began to coincide with the entire kingdom'

successors.note: The domain ceases to be a layer distinct from the kingdom when Navarre and Béarn are incorporated in 1620 (the last entry of the Crown lands chronology); from then the Kingdom of France dossier carries the land.

capitals.name: Paris
capitals.note: 'as Count of Paris, he made the city his power centre' (Hugh Capet page); the page does not call it a capital. Paris was under Burgundian control from May 1418 (Treaty of Troyes page), so the seat 1418-1421 is not stated.

capitals.name: Bourges
capitals.note: After Charles VI died in 1422 the Dauphin 'ruled the parts of France that rejected the treaty from Bourges'.

capitals.name: Paris
capitals.note: Treaty of Arras (1435) returned Paris to the king.

region.text: the royal domain at Hugh Capet's coronation: towns and estates between Paris and Orléans

ledger.note: 987: Hugh Capet is crowned king and the royal domain begins as his own lands between Paris and Orléans. 'Hugh was crowned rex Francorum on 1 June, in Noyon, and again on 3 July 987, in Paris'; 'Between Paris and Orléans he possessed towns and estates amounting to approximately 400 square miles (1,000 km2)'. The Crown lands page: 'the crown estate was extremely small and consisted mostly of scattered possessions'. Radii of 30 km are my drawing of 1,000 km2 of scattered estates.

minus.text: the County of Auxerre (Auxerre and its surroundings)

region.text: the County of Sens: the department of Yonne without Auxerre

ledger.note: 1055: the County of Sens is annexed to the domain. Page: 'annexation of the County of Sens'. The page names no holder; the department of Yonne is my reading of the county. [Fix 2026-10-25] The Auxerre disc is subtracted: the same Crown lands page has '1371: purchase of the County of Auxerre', so the department of Yonne no longer carries Auxerre before 1371.

1068: Gâtinais and Château-Landon pass from Fulk IV of Anjou to the king. Page: 'acquisition of Gâtinais and Château-Landon from Fulk IV, Count of Anjou'. The 30 km radius round Montargis is my reading of the Gâtinais.

1077: the French Vexin is annexed. Page: 'annexation of the French Vexin'. The Cliopatria County of Vexin shape (990-1084) is used for the land. [Fix 2026-10-25] Cliopatria's County of Vexin row runs 990-1084 (data/polities.csv); the Crown lands entry is 1077 and the domain draws the French Vexin from that year.
1101: the Viscounty of Bourges (with Dun-sur-Auron) is bought from Odo Arpin, the first foothold in Berry. Page: 'acquisition of the Viscounty of Bourges'.

region.text: the County of Amiens (Amiens, Montdidier, Roye)

ledger.note: July 1185: Philip II adds the County of Amiens by the Treaty of Boves. 'The first major increase to the royal demesne came in 1185, when Philip acquired the County of Amiens'; 'In July 1185, the Treaty of Boves left the disputed territory partitioned'. The Crown lands page adds Montdidier, Roye, Choisy-au-Bac and Thourotte. The page does not name the other party; the Count of Flanders is the Crown lands page's counterpart for the neighbouring Artois entry.

1191: the crown takes Péronne and its dependencies. County of Vermandois page: the Count of Flanders 'kept the county of Vermandois until his death, in 1191' and 'the king entered immediately into possession of Péronne and its dependencies'. Crown lands page, 1191 entry: the king acquired the County of Vermandois after Elisabeth's death, 'Confirmed in 1213'. The 40 km disc round Péronne is the land county-of-vermandois /ledger/5 draws for the crown. [Fix 2026-10-25] Replaces the whole-county gain of 1191: the east of the county was Eleanor's for life.

1200: the Norman Vexin, Évreux and Issoudun are annexed. Page: '1200: the Norman Vexin is annexed' and, as a second 1200 entry, 'the County of Évreux and Issoudun are annexed, in exchange for the king's recognition of John of England…'. The department of Eure is my reading of Évreux and the Norman Vexin; Issoudun lies in Berry, drawn by the Le Goulet event above.

region.text: Berry (Issoudun and the English possessions in Berry)

ledger.note: May 1200: by the Treaty of Le Goulet John gives up Berry. 'John agreed to heavy terms, including the abandonment of all the English possessions in Berry and 20,000 marks of silver.'

region.text: the Duchy of Normandy; Touraine; Anjou; Maine

ledger.note: 1204: Philip II confiscates Normandy, Touraine, Anjou and Saintonge from King John. Page: 'confiscation of the Duchy of Normandy, the Touraine, Anjou, Saintonge' (Poitou only temporarily). Philip II page: 'By the end of 1204, most of Normandy and the Angevin lands, including much of Aquitaine, had fallen into Philip's hands'; the Le Goulet terms named 'Anjou, Maine, and Touraine', hence Maine. Saintonge is not drawn (no region name).

region.text: the County of Vermandois without Péronne and its dependencies (Eleanor's life interest)

ledger.note: 1213: Eleanor of Vermandois dies and the rest of the county reaches the crown. County of Vermandois page: Eleanor had 'a life interest in the eastern part of Vermandois, together with the title of countess of St Quentin' and is dated '(d. 1213)'; the page does not describe the passing. Crown lands 1191 entry: 'Confirmed in 1213, by Eléonore of Vermandois'. county-of-vermandois /ledger/6 dissolves the county into the kingdom in June 1213 and draws the same land (shape of 1210 without the Péronne disc). [Fix 2026-10-25]

1223: Poitou is confiscated from the English. The Crown lands page's 1223 row lists the confiscation of Poitou, Saintonge, Angoumois, Périgord and part of the Bordelais; only Poitou is drawn here. [Fix 2026-10-25] Cliopatria's County of Poitou row runs 1206-1249 (data/polities.csv), against the Crown lands entries of 1223 (gain) and 1241 (loss to Alphonse); the dossier follows the page.

1223: Artois, held by Prince Louis since 1191, is integrated into the domain. Page: 'Artois given to Prince Louis (integrated only in 1223)'. [Fix 2026-10-25] Counterpart changed from county-of-artois, which exists only from 1237, to kingdom-of-france: Artois was the heir's own land inside the kingdom (given to Prince Louis in 1191) and joined the domain when he became king in 1223.

region.text: the sénéchaussées of Nîmes-Beaucaire and Béziers-Carcassonne

ledger.note: 1229: Raymond VII cedes lower Languedoc at the end of the Albigensian Crusade. Page: 'Raymond VII, Count of Toulouse cedes to the king the sénéchaussées of Nîmes – Beaucaire and of Béziers – Carcassonne' (Treaty of Paris); during the crusade (1209-1229) 'the king annexed the County of Toulouse'. The departments of Gard, Hérault and Aude are my reading of the two sénéchaussées.
1237: Artois becomes an appanage of Robert I. Page: '1237: the king confirms the appanage grant of the County of Artois for his brother Robert I of Artois.'

1241: Poitou becomes an appanage of Alphonse. Page: '1241: the king confirms the appanage grant of Poitou for his brother Alphonse, Count of Poitou.' Alphonse also held Auvergne, which the domain does not hold before 1271.

1246: Anjou becomes an apanage for Charles I of Anjou. Duchy of Anjou page: the county was 'turned into an apanage for the king's brother, Charles I of Anjou' (the page's sentence on the county's years in the domain runs 1205-1246). Maine is not mentioned on that page; the Crown lands 1225 entry assigns 'Anjou and Maine' together to Louis VIII's fourth son John and, on his death, to the seventh son Charles, and capetian-house-of-anjou /ledger/0 invests Charles with both in August 1246 (its Charles I of Anjou page). That dossier names kingdom-of-france as its source of the land, the layer this dossier sits in. [Fix 2026-10-25] Replaces the 1225 loss, which left Anjou and Maine ownerless until 1246.

notes:
Written for eu-10-x from eleven pages (Crown lands of France, Hugh Capet, Philip II of France, Treaty of Bretigny, Treaty of Troyes, Hundred Years' War, John Duke of Berry, Duchy of Berry, County of Ponthieu, Treaty of Arras 1435, County of La Marche). The Crown lands page has no infobox, no area and no capital, so no area comparison could be made and the keyframes carry no area figure. WebFetch returned its chronology as a summary table; the quotes in the notes are the short verbatim phrases it returned on a second request.
WHAT THIS DOSSIER IS: the lands the king held directly, a layer inside the Kingdom of France (Cliopatria 990-1791, dossier kingdom-of-france), which also draws vassal fiefs and apanages. The compile must draw this dossier over the kingdom's shape (or subtract it from it), as for duchy-of-francia.
KEYFRAMES: all are new (no Cliopatria row) and are generated from the ledger gains and losses, so each keyframe changes exactly when a ledger event does. Components are coarse: radii of 30-40 km round towns for the 11th-12th century acquisitions, departments for counties.
NOT DRAWN (page rows I did not use or could not place): Montreuil-sur-Mer 988 (marriage, 'first Capetian port'); Moret, Meulan, Gisors 1081-1187; Tournai 1187/1313; Alencon, Perche, Valois, Dreux, Nemours, Guines, Ostrevant, Bigorre, Comminges, Auxerre and similar castellany-sized rows; Burgundy 1034 (the page says it was given to Robert I in 1034 but not when the domain acquired it, so no gain is recorded; Kingdom of France carries 1003-1034); the Aquitaine given to Henry III in 1259 (not domain land); the Treaty of Corbeil 1258 (renunciation of Roussillon and Catalonia: no domain land moves); the Comtat Venaissin (named in the 1271 reversion; the 1274 entry has the king cede half of it to Pope Gregory X; no land is drawn for either); Comminges (1498 return, 'alienated in 1462'); Berry to Joan of France 1499 (no return date on the page, so Berry stays in the keyframes); the Brittany personal union before the 1532 union (not domain). Anjou and Maine leave in 1246, the Duchy of Anjou page's apanage date for Charles I of Anjou (the 1225 will date of the first draft left them ownerless); they return in 1328 and leave again at the letters patent of 25 October 1360. Touraine to Philip in 1361 (Crown lands: 'the king gives Touraine in appanage to his son Philip') is not drawn because no opened page dates its return; Montpellier after 1365 and the Dauphin's land 1422-1435 are not drawn either (the pages are silent).
CONFLICT: Brétigny page gives 8 and 10 May 1360 for drafting and 14 June and 24 October for ratification; the Hundred Years' War page says 8 May. The loss is placed in October (Calais ratification).
GAPS: the northern France held by the English 1420-1450 beyond Normandy and Paris (the Troyes page does not map it); the extent of the Dauphin's land 1422-1435; Angoulême after the 1360 cession (drawn again only from 1531, Counts and dukes of Angoulême page; no opened page dates the reconquest of the 1370s); Poitou 1360-1415 belongs to the duchy-of-berry dossier (John of Berry was count 1356/1357-1416) and re-enters the domain in 1416. The first draft had a 1378 domain gain of Poitou and Angoulême; it was removed after the John of Berry page showed Poitou was the duke's. Paris is regained in 1436 (Charles VII page, year only).
COUNTERPARTS WITHOUT DOSSIERS (flagged in the report): county-of-sens, viscounty-of-bourges, county-of-chartres, county-of-la-marche (Lusignan/Angouleme), duchy-of-berry, duchy-of-orleans, burgundian-state, pale-of-calais (the last three are written in this batch if they validate).
Gazetteer names the resolver may lack: Montargis, Abbeville, Boulogne-sur-Mer, Péronne (places); admin1 Gard, Hérault, Aude, Charente, Eure and Pyrénées-Atlantiques are Natural Earth names to check.

REPAIR 2026-10-25 (reviewer verdict fail, eu-10-x): (1) Anjou and Maine: 1225 loss replaced by 1246 loss to capetian-house-of-anjou, 1328 regain (from county-of-anjou, the Valois holder), 1360-10 loss to house-of-valois-anjou, 1480-7 regain of Anjou and 1481-12 regain of Maine (Duchy of Anjou page, Crown lands). The Duchy page puts Louis I's countship in 1350 and house-of-valois-anjou /ledger/0 puts it in 1356; this dossier follows the page's 1328/1360 sentence. (2) Paris: the 1418 loss to burgundian-state is gone; Paris is lost to kingdom-of-england at Troyes (21 May 1420) and regained in 1436.
